name: Port of Genoa (Stazione Marittima di Genova)
overview_text: Genoa is one of the most historically significant cruise ports in the Mediterranean and a key global homeport for MSC Cruises. Its primary passenger terminals sit directly alongside the historic center.
getting_around: The cruise terminal is only 500 meters from Genova Piazza Principe railway station and Principe Metro station, making public transit and walking straightforward.
all_aboard_warning: While the port is central and highly walkable, allow adequate time when navigating the narrow medieval caruggi alleys during evening departures.

terminals.name: Stazione Marittima - Ponte dei Mille
terminals.description: Historic, grand passenger terminal hub handling mega-cruise turnarounds with direct elevated gangway access.

terminals.name: Stazione Marittima - Ponte Andrea Doria
terminals.description: Secondary high-capacity passenger cruise terminal adjoining Ponte dei Mille.

terminals.name: Molo Vecchio Crociere
terminals.description: Boutique terminal in the Old Port basin handling superyachts and small luxury cruise liners up to 150m.

berths.name: Ponte dei Mille & Ponte Andrea Doria Quays
berths.notes: Multiple deep-water berths accommodating modern mega-cruise liners up to 340m length.
berths.source: Western Ligurian Sea Port Authority Berth Specifications

berths.name: Molo Vecchio Berths
berths.notes: Dedicated to luxury boutique ships and superyachts.

arrival_procedures: Direct alongside docking. Passenger processing is handled inside historic terminal structures that feature check-in desks, security, tourist information, and direct overhead gangway access. Genoa is a primary homeport for MSC Cruises.
departure_procedures: Efficient baggage drop-off and customs processing. The main terminal complex exits directly into a secure passenger plaza connecting to taxis and public roads.

walking_feasibility.description: Genova Piazza Principe Train Station is only 500 meters (5-10 minute flat walk) from the terminal. Reaching the Porto Antico aquarium and medieval caruggi takes 15-20 minutes on flat sidewalks.
